property_summary: The rule is: after any call to SetMinSum, if the call did not revert, MinSum must equal the argument passed; if it reverted, MinSum must be unchanged from before the call. The bug violates this because it sets MinSum before the revert check, so a reverting call to SetMinSum still changes MinSum.
After a call to SetMinSum that reverts, MinSum must remain unchanged from its previous value; the bug assigns MinSum before the revert check, so a reverting call to SetMinSum changes MinSum.

After any call to SetMinSum that does not revert, MinSum must equal the argument passed; after any call that reverts, MinSum must equal its value before the call. The buggy contract changes MinSum even when SetMinSum reverts.
For any caller and any argument, if SetMinSum reverts, MinSum must retain its pre-call value; the bug assigns MinSum before the revert check, so a reverting SetMinSum still changes MinSum.
After any call to SetMinSum that reverts, the contract's MinSum must remain unchanged; the bug assigns MinSum before the revert check, so a reverting call still changes MinSum.
LogFile can never be changed after Initialized() is called in the reference contract, but the mutant allows it to be overwritten by SetLogFile even after initialization.

In the reference implementation, calling LogFile.AddMessage always executes on a valid, deployed Log contract and therefore never reverts due to an extcodesize check when LogFile is set after initialization; in the mutant, LogFile can be overwritten after initialization with an EOA or a contract that reverts on AddMessage, causing future calls to LogFile-dependent functions to revert.

After any sequence of calls, if Initialized has been called, calling SetLogFile does not change the LogFile address in the reference, but the mutant allows it to change; the rule is: once Initialized is called, LogFile remains constant.
After calling SetLogFile, c.SetLogFile() returns the address of the new Log contract; in the reference it only applies before initialization, while the mutant allows it even after initialization.

After Initialized() is called and a non-zero _log is set, a subsequent SetLogFile call with a different non-zero _log must not change the LogFile address in the reference, but the mutant allows it to change.

For any deposit, the balance recorded for msg.sender must equal msg.value sent when the account was previously empty, not msg.value plus one extra wei; the buggy deposit adds an unexpected extra wei, breaking the equality.
For any call to Put, the recorded balance increment for msg.sender must equal the exact msg.value sent, but the bug adds one extra wei, breaking this equality.

After a successful Put, the contract's ETH balance must equal the sum of all users' recorded balances, but the bug adds an extra wei to the recorded balance without increasing the contract's ETH balance, breaking this invariant.

For any single Put call with nonzero msg.value by an account with zero prior balance, the recorded balance for that account must exactly equal msg.value in the reference contract; the buggy contract adds an extra wei, so the recorded balance equals msg.value + 1, violating this equality.

In the reference, for any Put where unlock time is not extended, the caller's balance after the call equals balance before + msg.value; the mutant increases balance by msg.value + 1, breaking this invariant.

After each Put, the unlock time of the sender must not decrease. The mutant deletes the unlock time update, so after a Put with a block.timestamp+_lockTime that would extend it, the unlock time stays smaller, which the reference preserves.

For any sequence of Put calls, the Collect function must succeed (not revert) for a sender who has sufficient balance and an unlock time in the past if and only if the sender's unlock time has correctly advanced past the current time; the mutant fails to update unlock time so Collect reverts when it should succeed.

For any user, after a Put call, if a subsequent Put call would extend the unlock time, the actual unlock time must be at least the original extension target; the mutant deletes the update so the unlock time remains unextended.

After any Put call, the sender's unlock time is always at least block.timestamp + the _lockTime argument of that call; the mutant never updates unlockTime, so this invariant fails when a Put would extend it.

After any Put call that would extend the sender's unlock time, their unlock time must be at least block.timestamp + _lockTime; the mutant never updates unlockTime, so this fails when a later Put extends it.

After consecutive Puts with increasing lock times, the unlockTime in the reference equals the maximum of the sum of timestamps and lock times, while in the mutant it equals only the last one, which can be smaller.
